newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-U.S. DAVIS CUP TEAM READY TO TACKLE BRAZILIAN CHALLENGE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-U.S. DAVIS CUP TEAM READY TO TACKLE BRAZILIAN CHALLENGE.

text.p: The United States introduced its Davis Cup tennis team for February's first-round tie against Brazil on Friday and captain Tom Gullikson said his squad would be up to the raucous away-court challenge.

Andre Agassi, Jim Courier, Todd Martin and Alex O'Brien comprise the team named by Gullikson for the February 7-9 tie in Ribeirao Preto against Brazil, whose last Cup opponent, Austria, quit a Sao Paulo tie because of rowdy fan behaviour.

"When the draw came out in October, I thought, 'Oh man, who's going to want to go down to Brazil, especially after what happened to the Austrian team and (Thomas) Muster,'" Gullikson told a news conference.
"But these guys stepped right up."

Muster, then ranked third in the world, stormed off court in the fifth set of doubles last September because of foul crowd behaviour. The Austrian, who said he had been spat at, and his teammates refused to play reverse singles Sunday, handing Brazil a 4-1 victory and a berth in the world group.
Besides a potentially hostile environment, this opening tie will require a quick transition from hard court to clay as the matches come 12 days after the end of the Australian Open.
"It's a difficult trip going down there from Australia, to make the transition to red clay and an incredibly unfriendly environment," said Gullikson. "These guys are up to the challenge."
The United States won the Cup for the 31st time in 1995, but were upset in the second round last year by the Czech Republic.

"I feel it is important to go down and make our presence felt," said Courier. "It won't be an easy match. We will have to be on top of our game. That's what sports is all about, going down to face the challenge."

"Davis Cup is certainly the most challenging competition as far as the mental side. You have people who clap at mistakes. These people are likely to try to blind us with mirrors, throw coins at us. They leave trash on practice courts....
"Don't give them any ideas," interrupted Agassi.
"When I go to baseball and basketball games I boo as much as anybody," continued Courier. "It's a rowdy, rough environment and you just try to rise above it."
U.S. Tennis Association president-elect Harry Marmion said he reviewed Austrian complaints about their treatment in Brazil and said the ITF believed that Muster overreacted to the fans.
"The ITF is concerned about what happened and will send their best officials," said Marmion, who said security needed to be tight to ensure as fair a tie as possible.
"We will provide our own security and take out one floor at our own hotel and provide our own transportation," he said.
Agassi, a member of Cup-winning U.S. teams in 1990, 1992 and 1995, expects to be refreshed for the Davis Cup after his decision to skip the Australian Open.
"I will be getting edgy to play by then," said Agassi, who has a 22-4 Davis Cup singles record.
As for edgy crowds, Agassi said he remembers being escorted to and from court during a Cup tie in Peru by men with guns. "That was certainly intense," he said.
Agassi warned of a different challenge to maintaining proper focus on the tennis court during the Brazilian tie.
"We are playing down there in summer time," Agassi said. "Those dental floss bikinis can be pretty distracting."
